# Pending changes (since patch 0015, 2026-11-20)

## 2026-11-20 - Stamina for the automaton

**Asked:** "add also for the automaton a ring similar to the fuel ring but this one is stamina, it depletes over time, faster when in combat, replenishes with food and energy drinks".

**Done:**
- New `Stamina` (scripts/stamina.gd): MAX 100, drains 100 per 600 s (a full ring = 10 calm minutes), x3 in a fight (hit in the last 4 s, holding the trigger or aiming). Any Food & drink good (14 of them: food, water, grain, wine, figs, cheese...) gives back 30, the new **Energy Drink** 60; 1.5 s between meals. Empty: walk at 60% speed and no health regen (a prompt says so once). Knocked out: back to at least 20.
- The surface gauge's outer ring (the ship's fuel ring, made configurable in HealthGauge: `fuel_name`, `fuel_liquid`, `fuel_rim`, `fuel_low_note`) shows stamina in green, its rim red below 20; the numbers in its tooltip.
- Pilot: `stamina`, `fighting()`, `tired()`, `walk_speed()`; the surface loads it from the player and writes it back each frame (`state.player.stamina`), PlayerData saves/loads it - kept between landings.
- Eating: `use_item` handles food and drinks (from the toolbar or a click in the field inventory); `Inventory.foot_usable()` replaces the FOOT_USABLE checks so food and drinks go on the foot toolbar (counts, cooldown curtain, tooltips).
- Energy Drink item (kind consumable, 25 dr, a green can with a lightning bolt icon): in station supplies (3 a purchase), chests, lockers and pirate loot; a new game starts with 3 in the hold.
- Docs: game.md "Stamina" bullet in the on-foot section; gauge tooltip explains the ring.
- Test: test_surface.test_stamina (drain x3 in a fight, food +30, drink +60, toolbar accepts food not ore, tired = slower + no healing, saved and loaded).

**Numbers:** 100 stamina, 0.167/s calm, 0.5/s fighting; food +30, drink +60; tired speed 60%; low below 20.

**Files:** scripts/stamina.gd (new), scripts/surface_props.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/health_gauge.gd, scripts/inventory.gd, scripts/items.gd, scripts/player_data.gd, scripts/station_menu.gd, scripts/surface_toolbar.gd, scripts/pages/field_inventory_page.gd (Stamina line in the pilot stats, toolbar hint), data/docs/game.md, tests/test_surface.gd, tests/test_inventory.gd (hold room with the starting drinks); shots retaken (surface_walk shows the ring).

## 2026-11-21 - The automaton and the pirates rebuilt in 3D: animated sprites, martial arts, the leap, the arcana, the Spell Book

**Asked:** "take the automaton sprite as reference and rebuild it in Blender as close as possible, make it render in all 8 isometric views at 30 fps. Keep the old sprite around as backup in case I want to restore it. Rig and animate it: regular walk cycles with or without a gun. Also a variety of martial art styles in the style of classic 80s beat 'em ups and one-on-one fighting games. Do the same for enemy NPCs. Give the automaton a jump animation that lets it quickly close distance to enemies and evade ranged attacks. Give it a variety of magic-like attacks - energy beams, fireballs, lightning strikes, energy domes, creation of minions - in the style of tabletop and computer RPGs. All these are skills that go on the 9-slot toolbar, with their own spell book and levelling system."

**Done - the art (external/blender/automaton/):**
- One android **kit** (kit.py): cel-shaded toon materials with an inverted-hull ink outline, rigid armour parts each on ONE bone (no weight painting), decals pressed onto parts (shrinkwrap, baked), an armature "Rig" of 24 bones (pelvis, spine, chest, head, pauldrons, upper / fore arms, hands, fingers, thighs, shins, feet, the rifle) under the empty "Root", and a **pose solver**: a pose is a handful of controls (pelvis shift / yaw / pitch / roll, chest twist / lean / bend, head, the hands' and feet's targets in chest / pelvis / world space with analytic two-bone IK, wrist bend, finger curl, the rifle's grip + muzzle direction with the hands following it, height off the ground).
- Two **skins** on that skeleton: `automaton.py` - you, rebuilt from external/images/player_on_foot_idle.png / _aim.png (cream armour over a dark slate frame, red triangle pauldrons, the forehead triangle, red ear rings, the chest light, red thigh and shin panels, the lights down the back and calves, the long cream-and-orange rifle with its scope); `pirate.py` - the pirate android from npc_pirate_frame_*.png (tan and bronze armour, a tricorn with gold trim and a skull, red eyes, a tattered crimson coat whose three tails hang on bones of their own and swing with the legs, skull pauldrons, a belt of pouches, cables down the back, a heavy rifle with glowing cells).
- **Animations** (moves.py, 30 fps, from key poses of the controls or worked out per frame): idle, guard (the fighting stance), walk (30 frames, 1.07 m a cycle), run (24 frames, 2.39 m), 13 martial arts moves - jab, cross, hook, uppercut, elbow, knee, front kick, side kick, roundhouse, spinning back kick, sweep, flying kick, force palm - the leap (a flip through the air), 4 casting poses (thrust, sky, dome, summon), hit, block, knock-out; with the rifle: idle, walk, run, raise, fire. Marks: the frame a blow lands, a spell lets go, the feet leave / touch the ground. Baked into both .blend files as 30 (automaton) / 20 (pirate) actions.
- **Rendering**: build.py / render_all.py - 8 Blenders at once, EEVEE, orthographic 22 degrees above, 100 px per metre, lights fixed to the camera, all 8 views of every frame: **4,232 pictures** for the automaton (529 frames) in 4 min, **2,120** for the pirate (265 frames). `tools/puppet_atlas.py` trims and packs them (identical pictures stored once: 3,399 / 1,704 different) into **13 + 7 atlas pages** of 2048 px (49.6 + 26.6 M px; BPTC on desktops: ~4 MB a page on the card) plus half-size sets for the web build (4 + 2 pages, lossless), with clips.json (each frame's page, rectangle and the point it stands on; marks, air heights, the muzzle and hands per view) -> art/player_clips/, art/pirate_clips/.

**Done - the game:**
- **SheetPuppet clip mode** (scripts/sheet_puppet.gd): a character with art/<id>_clips/ is drawn from its clips by the same controls as before (walk / phase pick a frame of the walk or run cycle by distance walked, raise_amt of "raise", release of "fire"), with the rifle in hand (`armed`) or bare hands (`stance` idle / guard), `gait` walk / run; `play(clip, speed, hold, reverse)` runs a clip once; `air()`, `point()`, `mark_time()`, `stride_px()`, `frozen` (hit pause). Pages load one at a time on the loading screen (ProcArt.warm -> SheetPuppet.warm_clips). **The old hand-drawn sheets stay** in art/player/ and art/pirate/: Settings > "Classic character sprites" (Settings.classic_sprites) draws them again (skills still work, without animations).
- **Skills** (scripts/skills.gd): 12 skills in 3 schools, on the toolbar as "skill:<id>" items.
  - Martial styles (chains of blows thrown while you attack in the style; blows stagger, kicks shove, finishers floor): Pygmachia (jab 14, cross 20, hook 24, uppercut 32), Pankration (elbow 19, knee 25, front kick 26, force palm 34), Laktisma (side kick 26, roundhouse 29 - all in front, spinning back kick 40). Techniques: Aspis Guard (60-80% of damage shrugged off, 1.5 s), Scythe Sweep (22, floors all around, 6 s cooldown), Comet Kick (45, a flying kick from 340 px, 7 s).
  - Movement: Hermes' Leap (a flip to where the mouse points, 380-470 px, 5 s cooldown; bolts fired at you in the air miss; from rank 3 the landing staggers).
  - Arcana: Phlox (fireball 44, bursts over 105 px, burns 4/s for 4 s), Helios Lance (beam 26 x 3 through all in a 720 px line), Keraunos (thunderbolt 60, stuns, leaps to 1-5 more at half), Aegis Dome (soaks 60-160 damage for 6-10 s, throws back those close), Eidola (1-3 spectral fighters for 18-24 s).
  - Levels: XP from kills (half the enemy's health, 8-400), blows (2) and spells (5) that land; 60 x level^1.3 XP a level, to level 20; a skill point a level (2 to start), spent to learn a skill (each needs a level: 1-10) or raise its rank (to 5: +20% damage, -7% cooldown a rank, and each skill's own rank lines). Every use costs stamina (1-12). Saved with the player ("skills").
- **Fighting** (scripts/planet_surface.gd, surface_props.gd): the Pilot has a `style` ("rifle" or a martial style) - clicking an enemy attacks in it: runs up (the run cycle), steps in and works through the chain; hit pause, sparks, shoves, staggers, knock-downs (enemies fall and get up: the fall played backwards). Spells are aimed at the enemy under the mouse / the one you fight / the nearest, else at the mouse's spot; gamepad: the way you face. New `scripts/skill_fx.gd`: sparks, kick arcs, rings, the beam, the fireball and its burst, the thunderbolt, the dome, the summoning circle, the charge in the hands (a few additive lines / discs each).
- **Pirates fight hand to hand**: within 100 px they sling the rifle and brawl (jab, cross, hook, uppercut, front kick, roundhouse, side kick, sweep: 5-11 damage, a blow every ~0.55 s), block a blow of yours now and then (22%: 65% of it gone); every third pirate is a brawler that charges from 420 px instead of shooting. Beaten, they fall with their own knock-out animation.
- **Spell Book**: the Field Computer's 7th tab (SKILLS, key K - a new rebindable action): level, XP bar, points; a row per skill (icon to drag / press 1-9, rank pips, Learn / Rank button), the hovered skill in full on the right. The toolbar shows skill icons (drawn in code), cooldown curtains, a mark under the style you fight in, and over it your level and an XP bar. New games start with Pygmachia, the Leap and Phlox on slots 4-6.
- 14 synthesised sounds (tools/sfx_skill.py -> sounds/skill/: whoosh, punch, kick, leap, land, guard, cast, beam, fire, burst, thunder, dome, summon, levelup; 29 takes, 259 KB).
- Docs: game.md - a new "Skills" page, controls, the Field Computer (7 tabs, K), pirates, settings; tutorial.md - a lesson "Skills: fists, the leap, spells"; shots skill_book and skills_fight (with notes). Export presets: desktop builds leave out the web atlases and the web build the desktop ones.
- Tests: tests/test_skills.gd (8: the clips, levels and learning, martial arts, leap and comet kick, spells, pirates brawling, the Spell Book, skills on the classic sprites); the three old sprite tests now run on the classic sheets; test_play's respawn test accepts either starting stack (kits or energy drinks) as the one lost.
- Area effects (sweep, roundhouse, bursts, the beam, the thunderbolt's leaps, the dome's and the landing's shock) hit enemies - and whatever you aimed at - not peaceful animals that stand near.
- A second pass on the models against the reference: slimmer limbs and boots, a smaller helmet, a wider stance, stronger two-tone shading, dark bands and panels, orange strips on shins and forearms, bigger eyes, a darker bulkier rifle.
- Tools: the FPS tour has two new scenarios per planet - "a brawl with skills (4 pirates, every blow and spell)" and "Field Computer, the Spell Book" (in tests/fps_baseline.json); tests/doc_shots.gd paces itself at 60 fps by the engine, not v-sync (a locked screen held a v-synced window at 1 frame a second), and loads Skills at run time.

**Numbers:** 2 skins, 24 bones, 30 clips (529 frames) + 20 clips (265 frames), 8 views, 30 fps -> 6,352 rendered frames, 5,103 different, 20 atlas pages (76.2 M px), ~80 MB of graphics memory; frame rate in a brawl with every skill: 456-482 fps on Thalassa (its plain wolf fight: 467-505), 690 Krystallos, 800 Selene, 939 Akrotiri, 1010 Kronos, no hitches (worst frame 3.5-7.8 ms); loading the atlases on the title screen: 253 ms in the background, one 41 ms frame (the second big texture reaching the card, once a run); automaton 189 px tall in the atlas (128 on screen). 12 skills, 13 blows, 5 ranks, 20 levels.

**Files:** external/blender/automaton/ (kit.py, automaton.py, pirate.py, moves.py, build.py, render_all.py, automaton.blend, pirate.blend - new), tools/puppet_atlas.py, tools/sfx_skill.py (new), art/player_clips/, art/pirate_clips/ (new), sounds/skill/ (new), scripts/skills.gd, scripts/skill_fx.gd, scripts/pages/skill_book_page.gd (new), scripts/sheet_puppet.gd, scripts/surface_props.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/surface_toolbar.gd, scripts/field_menu.gd, scripts/items.gd, scripts/inventory.gd, scripts/player_data.gd, scripts/settings.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, scripts/keybinds.gd, scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/loadout_panel.gd, scripts/pages/field_inventory_page.gd, export_presets.cfg, data/docs/game.md, data/docs/tutorial.md, data/docs/shots.json, tests/doc_shots.gd, tests/fps_tour.gd, tests/fps_baseline.json, tests/test_skills.gd (new), tests/test_surface.gd, tests/test_play.gd.

## 2026-11-21 - First steps to a 3D game: the automaton is its 3D model, the planets' ground is 3D geometry

**Asked:** "instead of a generated sprite replace it with the actual 3d model of the automaton - we will start slowly turning this to a 3D game", then "replace the terrain on planets with actual 3d geometry".

**Done - the automaton as its model:**
- Blender: `build.py -- automaton export` joins every part of the rigged model into ONE skinned mesh (each part's vertices held by its bone, the ink outlines kept as geometry - the inverted hull) and writes `art/player_3d/player.glb` (23,418 vertices, 11 materials, 21 bones, all 30 actions as animations, 3.0 MB) + `model.json` (per clip: frames, loop, marks, height off the ground per frame, the muzzle and hands as 3D points; the cel materials' colours / shade / highlight).
- `scripts/stage3d.gd` (Stage3D): one SubViewport with a 3D world of its own - a row of up to 4 cells (512 x 640 px at 135 px a metre), an orthographic camera at the sprites' angle (22 degrees), one light fixed to the camera, 4x MSAA; a character claims a cell and gets its model there, with the kit's cel shading remade as shaders (shaders/toon_part.gdshader: two hard tones + a highlight, flat_part.gdshader: lights and ink). Redrawn 60 times a second, only while it has characters; as wide as the cells in use. Models are loaded, made and drawn once (their shaders compiled) on the loading screen (ProcArt -> Stage3D.warm); freed cells keep their model.
- SheetPuppet **model mode**: the same controls and clips as the sprites (walk / phase, raise, fire, play(), marks, air), but the skeleton is posed at any moment in time (between the 30 keyed frames), a change of clip is blended over 0.11 s, and the model turns smoothly to ANY direction (16 / s), not just 8 views. The muzzle and hands are projected from their 3D points (within 3 px of the sprites', all 8 sides: tested). The rifle bone is scaled away in clips without it. If the stage is full the sprites stand in.
- Settings > "Characters drawn from": 3D model (default) / Rendered sprites / Classic sprites (replaces yesterday's "Classic character sprites" switch; Settings.character_graphics). Pirates and eidola are still drawn from their rendered sprites.

**Done - the ground as 3D geometry (`scripts/ground3d.gd`, Ground3D):**
- The streamed worlds' ground is no longer tile pictures laid over each other (TileMapLayers drawn as GroundChunks' pictures) but MESHES: a tile on level l is a 1 x 1 square at that height (a level = 0.4976 units = 39 px on screen), a cliff block its top and its two front faces a level deep, a ramp the square tilted up a level with faces under it. One mesh per generated chunk of the world (32 x 32 tiles; its arrays worked out on a worker thread as the chunk arrives - PlanetSurface._take_step -> add_chunk - the mesh made on the main thread, 2 a frame, 6 under the landing's veil).
- Textured from the same pieces (the tile set's atlas): each vertex takes the pixel it had in its piece's picture, so from the game's view the ground looks as it did - but heights are real and cliffs hide what's behind them by depth (the 2D layers used to paint whole cliff blocks over higher ground in front of them: those stray cubes are gone).
- An orthographic Camera3D at the isometric angle (30 degrees above the horizon, turned 45: a tile's square is the 128 x 64 px diamond; 90.51 px a unit) follows the 2D camera; the picture - a SubViewport the size of the window + 128 px all round, drawn again only when the view leaves it, the zoom changes or the ground does - is shown by a sprite where the 2D ground was (z -10): everything else of the 2D world is drawn over it as before. Tested to be within 1 px of where the 2D ground drew each tile.
- Sharper when zoomed (drawn at the zoom, not a scaled picture). No tile layers or ground pictures are made any more when it's on (PlanetSurface.ground3d; tile_ground / ground_chunks stay null).
- Settings > "3D terrain" (Settings.terrain_3d; off: the 2D tiles as before); dev switches SA_GROUND2D=1 / SA_SPRITES=1 (environment) to compare. Planets built whole (a saved layout) and non-tiled worlds keep the 2D ground.

**Numbers (Thalassa, a quiet machine; everything 2D - rendered sprites, 2D ground - / both 3D):** idle 718 / 699 fps, walking 594 / 595, a wolf pack 443 / 446, the skills brawl 479 / 438, inside a building 614 / 569, Field Computer inventory 817 / 718, map 709 / 696, Spell Book 741 / 701, cargo transfer 1135 / 1123. No hitches in either (worst frame 13 ms). An earlier run with another game open showed 53-61 ms frames in both variants: that was the other game.

**Tests:** test_skills.test_model_puppet (the model, its clips' parity with the sprites', smooth turning, the muzzle from 8 sides, the leap, the stage's cells, the fallbacks), test_skills.test_ground_3d (a mesh a chunk, real heights, pixel-exact against the 2D ground, no redraw for the same view, the 2D fallback); the three tests of the 2D tile layers run with Ground3D off.

**Files:** external/blender/automaton/build.py (export), art/player_3d/ (new: player.glb, model.json), scripts/stage3d.gd, scripts/ground3d.gd, shaders/toon_part.gdshader, shaders/flat_part.gdshader (new), scripts/sheet_puppet.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/settings.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_skills.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, tests/test_gas_giant.gd, tests/test_frame_budget.gd; shots retaken.

## 2026-11-21 - The 3D ground: its sliding fixed, its tiles modelled in 3D

**Asked:** "the terrain randomly shifts around, fix it, replace the terrain tiles with 3d ones" (and, in Blender: "open blender with the new 3d automaton and its animations"; "I am trying to change the action in the action editor but it always only plays back the walk animation, why?").

**Done:**
- **The sliding:** the 3D camera is moved just before a frame is drawn, but a 3D node's move reaches the renderer a step later than a 2D one's - so after each redraw the ground's picture was drawn from where the camera WAS and shown where it is, and stayed offset until the next redraw. Fixed: `_cam.force_update_transform()` (Ground3D.sync). Checked in a window: markers on tile centres stay on their tiles while walking.
- **3D tiles** (Ground3D._work): a tile is no longer a flat square carrying its painted picture but a small model - the ground a 3 x 3-point patch that rolls with one smooth relief field over the whole world (RELIEF 0.035 units, ~3 px: tiles and chunks meet), with normals; a cliff block's two front faces built of stone blocks in two courses (5 a face: each a bevelled block standing 0.035-0.085 out of a dark wall, in its own shade of the tile set's stone); a bank under every patch's front edges (1.45 levels deep: seen where the ground in front is lower - shores no longer open onto nothing); stone under a ramp's sides; water a sheet sunk 0.32 of a level below the shore. Two surfaces a chunk: the patches (the tiles' pictures as albedo) and the stone (vertex colours).
- **Lit by a real sun** (DirectionalLight3D from the upper left of the screen, as the painted scenery is lit; ambient 0.62 + sun 0.52: tops as bright as before, left faces lit, right faces in shade) that casts shadows (orthogonal, 120 units; the camera stands 60 back).
- A chunk arriving out of sight no longer redraws the picture (the world is made all round you for minutes after landing: each arrival used to redraw it).
- **Blender:** external/blender/automaton/open_anim.py opens a skin's .blend ready to look at its animations (the rig active, "walk" playing, the timeline as long as the action picked). The armour's 163 parts are now unselectable (kit.rig_parts, open_anim.py): a click on the model used to make a PART the active object, and the Action Editor then changed that part's action - the rig went on playing "walk".

**Numbers:** a 32 x 32-tile chunk: ~9,200 patch vertices + its stone; frame rate measured with Blender playing an animation on the same card (noisy: +-8% run to run) - Thalassa, all 2D / 3D ground only / both 3D: idle 654 / 643 / 632, walking 581 / 560 / 506, wolf pack 393 / 388 / 377, brawl 448 / 399 / 401, building 539 / 528 / 465; to be re-measured on a quiet machine.

**Files:** scripts/ground3d.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, tests/test_skills.gd, external/blender/automaton/open_anim.py (new), external/blender/automaton/kit.py; shot surface_walk retaken.

## 2026-11-21 - The automaton in a few main parts; its 3D model in the inventory, turned by dragging

**Asked:** "the automaton is made out of too many parts, merge the majority of them and keep only a few main ones, I want to be able to easily select them and edit them in Blender. Also in game in the inventory use the actual 3D model and allow me to rotate it with left click and dragging."

**Done:**
- **Blender (external/blender/automaton/):** kit.merge_parts() (called by `build.py -- <skin> model` after rig_parts) joins the rigid pieces into the REGIONS' main parts - automaton: 163 pieces -> 7 (Head, Torso, Arm.L, Arm.R, Leg.L, Leg.R, Rifle); pirate: 8 (+ Coat, its tails). Each part is a skinned mesh (an Armature modifier; each piece's vertices in its bone's vertex group), its bevels and thickness applied, its outline one Ink modifier (the inverted hull) whose thickness per piece is kept as the "ink" vertex group's weight - the model looks exactly as before. The old many-part files are kept in backup/ (automaton_163parts.blend, pirate_many_parts.blend). All actions baked again (30 / 17). `build.py export` takes the skinned parts (their outlines made geometry, the bone groups kept); open_anim.py: an action picked in the Action Editor while a part is the active object is handed to the rig (the parts stay selectable for editing). kit.preview() clears the rig's action before posing (contact sheets of a baked .blend showed one frame).
- **The game:** new `scripts/model_view.gd` (ModelView): the character's actual 3D model in a menu - Stage3D's model and cel shaders in a little 3D world of its own, in its idle animation, drawn 30 times a second while it's on screen. Drag with the left button to turn it round (and a little up and down); it keeps its turn from one opening to the next. EquipDoll takes it in place of the picture (`view`); LoadoutPanel uses it - the Field Computer's and the Ship Computer's inventories. Not drawn from models (Settings): the picture as before.
- Test: test_skills.test_model_view; shots computer_inventory and field_inventory retaken.

**Files:** external/blender/automaton/kit.py, build.py, open_anim.py, automaton.blend, pirate.blend, backup/ (new), art/player_3d/player.glb (re-exported: 25,912 vertices), scripts/model_view.gd (new), scripts/equip_doll.gd, scripts/loadout_panel.gd, tests/test_skills.gd.

## 2026-11-21 - 3D space, stage 1: a star system in 3D, planets of real procedural ground

**Asked:** "time to redesign the entire game into a 3D game. I want everything to be 3D: solar systems, planets, stations, spaceships, creatures, monsters, NPCs. I want to play everything from a third-person camera, with heavy use of procedural generation. Do this in stages, letting me taste and test the game at each stage." - and, while it was being built: "landing on a planet should be completely procedural" (seamless, from orbit to the ground).

**The plan (stages):** 1 - space in 3D (this entry); 2 - landing and walking on the planets as the 3D automaton, from orbit without a break; 3 - life on them: procedural plants, creatures, monsters, people; 4 - stations, docking, NPC ships, combat in 3D; 5 - the whole game moved over (galaxy, saves, missions, economy) and the 2D game retired. The 2D game stays as it is meanwhile; the 3D one starts from the title screen.

**Done (stage 1):**
- **Title screen:** "3D Space (preview)" (main_menu._on_space3d): a galaxy charted under the veil if there's none, then `scenes/cosmos.tscn`.
- **Cosmos** (scripts/cosmos/cosmos.gd): the current system of the galaxy (Galaxy's systems - the 2D game's planets, moons, stations, gates, asteroid fields; the home system's planets from main.gd's HOME_ORBITS) built in 3D at 10 m a map unit, a piece a frame under the loading veil (build_settled: every planet's first patches in). Floating origin: the world moves back whenever the ship strays 2.5 km from the middle - precise at any distance (the system is ~130 km across). Sky: stars, the galaxy's band and nebulae from one shader (sky.gdshader). One sun light, turned each frame to shine from the star onto the ship (shadows within 900 m, the first split 36 m); every planet is lit from its own direction to the star (its shaders' light()).
- **Planets of real ground** (CosmosPlanet + PlanetShape): one height field a planet (FastNoiseLite: domain-warped continents, ridged ranges, craters on moons, hills and the ground underfoot - its PlanetGen look's colours, water level, ice, lava, clouds: the 2D planet's palette). The sphere is a cube's six faces bent round, each a quadtree of 16 x 16-quad patches built on worker threads: far off 6 patches, coming closer they split (closer than 1.7 sizes; merge back past 2.1) down to ~22 m patches (~1.4 m a quad) - the planet seen from orbit IS the ground you fly down to. Children replace a parent only when all four are built (no holes); skirts hide the seams between levels; patches behind the horizon aren't drawn; meshes made within 1.5 ms a frame (all planets). Seas (water with waves and the sun's glint, an ice sheet, or lava), a cloud shell, and an atmosphere shell worked out per pixel against the depth buffer (the halo from space, a blue sky with sunset colours on the ground, haze over distance). Gas giants: banded clouds with a storm, rings with the planet's shadow.
- **Star** (glowing, boiling surface + two glows), **stations** (procedural: hub, turning ring on spokes, modules, solar wings, lit bay, beacon - in the empire's colours, varied by seed), **gates** (a ring with a swirling field: fly through to jump - the next system built the same way, you arrive at its gate back), **asteroid fields** (320 tumbling rocks a field: three lumpy meshes drawn as multimeshes).
- **Your ship** (CosmosShip): a procedural hull (lofted fuselage, swept wings, twin engines with glowing nozzles and plumes, canopy, fins, the empire's stripe). Flight: the mouse is a virtual stick (pitch/yaw rate by its offset; C centres), A/D roll, W/S throttle (it stays), X stop, Shift boost (180 m/s, 470 boosting); J cruise drive - 1.6 s charge, then top speed = 0.55 x the clearance to the nearest planet/station/gate a second (600 m/s .. 40 km/s), so it slows by itself and drops out ~1.1 km from things. Bumps: the ground (it skims along it), stations, rocks, the star. Gamepad: left stick, triggers, A boost, Y cruise.
- **Camera** (CosmosCam): third person behind and above, turning after the ship a moment late, wider with speed; wheel zoom, right button looks round; never under the ground. **HUD** (CosmosHud): markers with distances, the target boxed / an arrow at the screen's edge (T targets what's nearest the middle), stick reticle, speed, throttle, drive state, altitude over the nearest planet, controls (H). **Esc**: Resume / Back to the title screen.
- **No long frames:** CosmosWarm (at the title screen, with Warmup) makes the noise texture (64^3, tiling, on a worker), the shared unit spheres (seas, clouds, atmospheres, gas giants are scaled unit spheres) and draws one of every 3D material in a small off-screen viewport set up like the scene (shaders compiled, pipelines and shadow passes made) and the HUD's text sizes.

Your ship: shields (regenerating) and hull, twin lasers (left button; the HUD's lead ring on a targeted ship), bounties; CosmosBoom explosions; lose your ship -> back by the first station. **Docking** (F near a station): traffic control flies you under the bay and up into it (fade) -> **CosmosHangar**: a procedural hall (pad with light rings, the bay's field, light panels, cargo, a crane, crew automatons walking about, 5 terminals); the walker's deck mode; L/Space aboard undocks.

## 2026-11-21 - Big stations: landing pads, docking by hand, traders on the pads, solid parts

**Asked:** "the stations also need to be large enough to accommodate docking of several NPC ships including much larger ones, also docking should be manual with the player flying and landing the ship precisely".

**Done:**
- **The station** (CosmosStation) rebuilt big - ~2-2.5 km across - from modular pieces by its seed and empire (its STYLE: hull, dark and paint colours, the empire's accent for the lights): a core tower of stacked sections with bands of windows, a slowly turning habitat ring of 36 segments on 4 spokes, 4 docking arms each ending in a platform - two with 3 small pads (90 m), two with one big pad (230 m: the biggest freighters) - numbered, edged with lights, floodlit; solar wings, a mast and beacon. ~250 parts merged into one mesh per material (and one per pad's lights): ~12 draw calls a station.
- **Docking by hand:** F near a station asks it for a pad (the smallest free one that takes your ship; F again cancels) - it lights up, marked on the HUD (an arrow at the edge when off screen). Thrusters: Space / Ctrl up and down, Q / E sideways (45 m/s). Over the pad the readout shows the height, the drift off its middle and the speed; set down inside it, level, under 12 m/s -> touchdown; the pad's lift takes the ship 60 m down (2.5 s, fading) into the hangar. Undocking: up the lift onto the pad, off it - the pad freed once you're clear. (Tests and tours use the docking computer: request_dock(true) flies it over the pad, the same touchdown follows.)
- **Traffic on the pads:** traders bound for a station ask for a pad, fly over it, come down level, sit 25-60 s, lift off and head for their next stop; 60% of the traders near a station are bound for it. A new **hauler** class (9x a fighter: ~170 m, slow) that only the big pads take.
- **Solid stations:** the ship bumps into the station's parts themselves (boxes and cylinders, three points along its hull) - hit one faster than 40 m/s and the hull takes it; the other ships too; the camera stops at them (CosmosStation.cam_hit).
- **Fixes:** the floating origin moving under a landing / take-off / the docking computer (their ends are moved with it).

**Numbers:** a station: ~250 parts -> ~12 meshes; 8 pads (6 x 90 m, 2 x 230 m); built in ~6 ms (one loading step a station). Scene nodes by the station 1221 -> 598. (Frame rate not re-measured yet: the machine was busy.)

**Tests:** test_cosmos: docking via the pad and the lift (and undocking up it), a hand-flown touchdown on the thrusters, the station's parts solid (flown at the core: held off), a trader flying in and sitting on a pad. Doc shot space3d_pad (new), space3d_hangar retaken (out on the hangar's deck), the guide's Stations / Docking paragraphs rewritten.

Assembled from modular pieces: the **palace** - wings of 1-3 storeys round a 36 x 24 m court (stepped masses, base courses, a fresco band and a cornice each storey, windows, parapets, horns of consecration), a colonnade of Aegean columns (dark base, shaft wider at the top, cushion capital and abacus), gateways, an altar with horns, a grand staircase up onto the roofs; **houses** on 13 m lots along lanes (1-3 storeys, a door, windows, now and then an upper storey, a roof pergola or horns), gardens with storage jars; a **shrine** (three rooms, the middle tallest, columns, horns), a **storehouse** with rows of pithoi; a paved square and a **landing field** beside the town. Every piece a box or a column in the town's frame - all ONE mesh (built on a worker; ~28k triangles a city) in one shader (building.gdshader: the slots - walls, stone, gypsum, columns, capitals, frescos, trim, doors, horns, wood, jars, roofs - are its parameters: the empire's palette from BuildingLook's themes; plaster mottling, grime near the ground). - **Their lairs:** the system's monster signals (Galaxy.signals_in - "Unknown bio-signature (Hard)") on the HUD; within 9 km the creature is out; it swims round its lair, comes for you within 3.5 km, keeps its distance and attacks in telegraphed patterns of slow glowing orbs (ring round you with a gap in the middle, fan, spiral, bloom - 260 m/s, your hitbox 12 m), rams; hit anywhere along its body (spheres along its spine). Slain: a bounty (4000 dr x its level), the signal done.

**Numbers:** a city: 357 solid blocks, ~28k triangles, one draw; 153 walkable spots; the levelled ground within 0.00 m of the town's plane. A monster: one mesh, one draw, 4-20 hit spheres. (Frame rate to be measured: the machine was busy.)

- **On foot, fewer markers:** your ship, the towns, your target and what's within 5 km (not every gate and signature in the system); a town's own marker hidden while you're in it.
- **Hunters come down to bite:** flying and floating predators drop low when they hunt.
- **Fixes:** freed citizens no longer read (an error each tick as people were let go); the doc shots and the frame-rate tour walk down the ramp (they had been standing in the cockpit "on foot") and out from under the ship.
- **Doc shots:** space3d_town (a palace's court in daylight, its people) and space3d_monster (Cerberus) taken; the rest retaken and their notes redone for the 3D HUD.

All three of its weapons on their own materials - the laser rifle, the laser bow (gold limbs, a string and an arrow of light, a quiver on the back) and the labrys (a red haft, two gold-rimmed blades with spirals, edges of light): one model, the game shows one.
  - **The palace guard** (guard.py): the android's build in the guard's palette - terracotta and ochre ceramic, a dark red frame, the fan crest in red and blue, a glowing orange core, a laser rifle, no cape.
  - **Kilon Alios** (kilon.py): a deep hood with two orange eyes in its shadow, a long dark coat to the ankles (its tails on bones), gold trims, belt and straps, steel arms, heavy boots.

- **Photoreal at the source:** the kit's materials are physically based now (Principled BSDF: colour, metal and roughness by part - the game's rules) and the ink outlines are gone (kit.INK = 0; the old cel kit kept in backup/kit_toon.py); the previews lit by a sun, a fill and a rim over a sky, AgX. The automaton and the pirate rebuilt the same way (their files lighter: no outline geometry - the pirate 65k -> 33k vertices).
- **In the game** (CosmosNpc citizens): a Minoan town's people are its palace guards and its androids (rifle, bow or labrys); other empires' towns have the android in their colours (its armour / accent / glow slots - the materials named for it). Armed townsfolk take on pirates and hunting beasts within 45 m (rifle and bow fire bolts; the labrys runs in and strikes). CosmosModels.apply's `hide` leaves out a model's parts by material (the weapons). CosmosWarm makes every variant at the title.
- **Kilon Alios** waits by every city's landing field, turning to watch you; E beside him opens his conversation (QuestData.GIVER - the 2D game's lines and voices, the story's dialogue box with his portrait): his greeting, then a menu in the game's theme - who he is, who you are, where you are, your mission, what you may become, the main quest (offered: accept / not now; or how it goes) and farewell.

## 2026-11-21 - Frame rate: the towns' levelling packed, anti-aliasing and bloom cheaper

**Done:**
- **PlanetShape.height** (hundreds of calls a frame as the ground refines): the towns' levelling read an array of arrays with conversions on every call - roughly doubling its cost; now packed arrays (set_flats()).
- **Anti-aliasing:** the MSAA modes no longer add FXAA on top (it only blurred, at its own cost: ~0.07 ms); Settings > Anti-aliasing reads "MSAA 2x / 4x / 8x".
- **Bloom:** linear upscaling instead of bicubic (~0.05 ms a frame, as soft).

**Numbers (fps_test.py 3d, quiet machine, RTX 2070 SUPER):** by the station 819, over an ocean world ~850, low over the sea 582 (p95 3.1 ms), over a volcanic world 693, on foot 624, a pirate camp fight 666, walking through a town 583, the Hyperion drive 921, a dogfight 778, a space monster's attack ~930, the hangar ~820. GPU 0.9-1.5 ms a frame (bloom ~0.35 ms, AA ~0.1 ms); the p95 frames are the ground's patch commits and LOD visits - still under the 600 bar at p95 in most scenarios: the next work.

## 2026-11-21 - The sky from your ship, landing on small worlds

**Asked:** "when I land on a planet and climb back the ramp of my spaceship the atmosphere disappears and I see empty space with the starfield"; "some planets are too small to land, it complains that the terrain is not even".

**Done:**
- **The sky stays on board:** inside your ship the atmosphere and clouds were switched off (so they'd never show through the hull) - you saw the bare starfield through the ramp and canopy. The air already stops at the hull (it reads the depth buffer), so the shells now stay on; only docked in a hangar are they off.
- **Landing on small and icy worlds:** the check sampled the ground 16 m out (4 m of rise allowed) - on the small moons the crater rims failed it at about 70% of spots, and on ice worlds it measured the ground under the ice sheet while the ramp measured the ice, failing "too uneven for the ramp" at about 60%. Now: the ship sets down on the ice sheet (Cosmos.set_down_h), the hull's footprint is checked (10 m round, 3.5 m), and when the spot right under you won't do, L finds the nearest good ground within 150 m (rings round you, turned either way) and sets down there - "Can't land" only when there's none. The same checks pick the spot a called ship comes down on. Found once per 0.3 s or 6 m (the HUD asks every frame).
- **A freed ramp:** the ship's interior no longer poses its ramp while being freed (an error on jumping between systems).

**Numbers:** over 30-120 dry spots a world in two systems: right under you OK - ice worlds 15% -> 55-85%, moons 10-25% -> 25-40%; somewhere within 150 m - every spot on every world.

**Tests:** test_cosmos.test_land_on_any_world (new). Doc shots retaken.

**Files:** scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd (landing_check, _spot_why, land_spot, set_down_h, land, _landing_spot_near, the shells), scripts/world/player/cosmos_ship_interior.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd.
